original_target.title: Can bounded complementary components of balls be controlled uniformly under nonnegative Ricci curvature?

full_original_statement:
For each dimension $`m`$, does there exist a constant $`\mu_m\in(0,1)`$ with the following property? For every complete, connected, noncompact $`m`$-dimensional Riemannian manifold $`M`$ with $`\mathrm{Ric}_M\geq0`$, every basepoint $`o\in M`$, and every $`r>0`$, each **bounded connected component** of $`M\setminus B_o(r)`$ lies in an **unbounded connected component** of $`M\setminus B_o(\mu_m r)`$.

The constant must depend on the dimension alone, not on the manifold, basepoint or radius. The question concerns the depth of bounded components of a ball's complement; having only one end does not itself give this uniform quantitative containment.

sources.scope_comparison: The local target requires a constant depending only on dimension for every complete Ricci-nonnegative manifold, every center and scale, controlling all bounded complement components. The inspected primary Proposition 0.3 adds a reverse-volume-doubling condition with exponent nu>p and constants Co,CP,CD; its connectivity factor depends on these data. One-endedness explicitly says nothing about bounded components. This is a restricted sufficient condition, not the dimension-only conclusion. The 2021 source Remark 4.18 author PDF could not be retrieved; no later matching full claim was found in the bounded searches.
